Karassk (L68) / Khatalashya (S81) Campaign Chain

Region (English scoring-table division): Sarhal.

Starting country: Karassk (L68) Formable country: Khatalashya (S81)

In brief: This is a very long antagonist campaign that takes a declining naval empire toward the “333rd Empire” and interstellar war. Early on, you must restore the empire amid wars on two fronts, debt, and competition for naval and land resources; after formation, the story turns to naga rule, mutation management, spire colonisation, and a Hive-Mind crisis. There is a great deal here, but both halves are mechanically demanding.

Story: very high｜Mission-tree length: very long (35 direct L68 missions and 48 direct S81 missions)｜Mission-tree update: verified for local v1.37.5.0｜Distinctiveness: very high｜Tedium: high｜Early pressure: very high｜Expansion: high

Identity and History

Karassk (L68) is a country present at the 1444 start; Khatalashya (S81) is its formable successor. The current local Chinese localisation displays them as “卡拉斯克” and “卡塔拉什亚,” respectively. The local English name of the starting country is Karassk; Khatalashya is the successor's name (also written Katalashya in some older material). 【Local scripts】【Local Chinese localisation】

Karassk is predominantly Lizardfolk, follows Anzalkatsa, and has a monarchy with a unique reform. In 1444 it is ruled by Krorasz V of the Godseeker dynasty and is a long-standing enemy of Zerat, Chanizad and Rayaz. 【Local history script】

Official material describes the old empire as a great power stretching from Konololo to Najni. Civil war, the accidental destruction of the Ashuzhal Spire, the loss of naga support, Kheteratan invasion, debt, and the increasing use of foreign troops drove its decline. By 1444, rebels threatened the capital from both north and south, and the country was fighting two unfavourable wars at once. 【Official dev diary】

National Story and Campaign Arc

Karassk does not see itself as a small country waiting for a restoration; it refuses to accept that the old empire has fallen. It places human descendants under the administration of the Khair families, treats the halfling islands and merfolk settlements as dependencies to be brought back into order, and uses tribute, enslavement, and terror to reclaim its former reach. 【Local narrative text】

To form Khatalashya, the country must be at peace and independent or tributary, retain its Lizardfolk and Anzalkatsa identity, own at least 75 provinces in Taneyas, and control at least 6 key provinces. Karassk is also subject to a country-specific flag: it must complete its late-campaign event before forming. 【Local script】

After formation, the mission tree is replaced as a whole. The country must do more than restore the old empire: it must prove the “333rd Empire” prophecy, unify the naga system, control mutations, exploit ancient spires, and extend the empire to other worlds. L68 and S81 are linked through historical Tags and a small number of compatibility events, not a shared mission set.

Core Mechanics

The Khair families and population governance. Karassk incorporates some human descendants into the Lizardfolk order in a legal sense while retaining pronounced inequality. Missions combine family politics, migration, cultural management, and imperial stability; this is the central governance theme before formation. 【Local script】

Naval power, tribute, and terror. Heavy ships, transports, marines, merfolk labour, and coastal construction all appear as mission requirements. The country can also rebuild its tributary network, raid targets, and compel other Lizardfolk to submit, so its army, navy, and treasury must all function at once. 【Local script】

Prophetic legitimacy and naga rule. S81 has several tiers of “belief in the prophecy” modifiers and must unite two centres of naga power. If progress is too slow, the legitimacy of the “Final Empire” comes under question. Proving the prophecy, rather than simply continuing to expand, becomes the core domestic task after formation. 【Local script】

Mutations and the Blood Curse. Khatalashya can deliberately manage several mutations and can raise the number maintained simultaneously by ending the Blood Curse. Different mutations support administration, warfare, colonisation, and crisis response; restoring the Dark Marshes also connects the repair of the old empire's wounds to this system. 【Local script】

Spire colonisation and the Hive-Mind war. The late game requires restoring ancient spires and maintaining several colonies in other worlds, before confronting a Hive-Mind disaster. During the crisis, the country suffers severe unrest, morale, and organisation penalties and temporarily cannot declare ordinary wars; it must retake the spire and destroy the enemy core. 【Local script】

Campaign by Stage

Opening: Relieve pressure on the capital and keep the two-front armies from collapsing separately. The straits, fleet, and diplomacy must all serve survival; if you build as though this were a land power alone, heavy ships, sailors, and transports will create a concentrated resource burden later.

Restoration: Gradually recover old colonies and coasts, and establish Khair administration and a tributary network. Do not form before completing Karassk's missions: the country-specific flag will otherwise lock the decision.

Preparing to form: Plan wars around the 75-province threshold, the 6 key provinces, and a window of peace. Since S81 replaces the entire tree, finish Karassk-specific merfolk, canal, and imperial-restoration objectives first.

The 333rd Empire: After formation, stabilise prophetic belief and naga administration before tackling mutations, the Blood Curse, the Dark Marshes, and overseas colonisation. The mission span quickly reaches from Taneyas to Aelantir and other worlds; forming the country does not end the economic and naval pressures.

Endgame: Complete the spire and colonial network, and reserve stability, troops, and crisis forces for the Hive-Mind. Formation is not an automatic victory; it is the campaign's second act.

Formable Country and Endgame

Khatalashya has 5 groups and 48 direct missions. Its main arc can be summarised as rebuilding the empire, establishing naga rule, proclaiming the prophecy fulfilled, controlling mutations and the Blood Curse, and creating an interstellar empire before confronting the Hive-Mind. 【Local script】

“Eternal Empire” is not an uncomplicated declaration of triumph. The endgame text asks whether an interstellar civilisation will repeat the same cycles of rise and fall, suggesting that the 333rd Empire may be another imperial myth. The Hive-Mind route also has a separate country-name ending. 【Local narrative text】

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 90/100｜Authoritarianism 90/100｜Magic↔Artifice 40/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 65/100)｜Pluralism 15/100.

The v2.1 value rating is Evil (9/100), with a stable trajectory. Enslavement, terror politics, forced mutation, and highly instrumental population governance are central institutions; the very low rating reflects concrete violations of personhood, not imperial expansion.

Recommended for players who enjoy an antagonist's imperial restoration, combined land and naval warfare, population governance, a formable-country transition, disasters, and a science-fiction endgame. Not recommended for players who dislike enslavement narratives, a two-front opening, naval construction, long mission locks, or complex late-game systems.

Community Experience

【Community view】A 2026 Khatalashya campaign report says the mission line can extend into the 1700s and highlights the late-game disaster, space colonisation, naga agenda, and combined naval and land warfare. The author did not identify submods, so these mechanics claims do not supersede the local scripts.

【Community view】A more recent Karassk discussion recommends first lifting the capital siege, using straits and the fleet to divide the two enemy fronts, and scheduling the naga agenda carefully. The post reflects the Insyaa update context; values and optimal routes may change with hotfixes.

Evidence Boundaries

This article concerns the local base Mod and localisation for v1.37.5.0, checked on 16 September 2026. The 35 L68 missions, 48 S81 missions, formation lock, core mechanics, and Hive-Mind disaster are confirmed in current local scripts; every reward and random event has not been audited individually.

Eight official Reddit materials of varying strength were recorded using the established combinations of names, Tags, formable country, and core mechanics. Diary #92 is the central feature; the others add historical context, release status, or authorship only. The complete offline Wiki has no dedicated article for Karassk, Katalashya, or Khatalashya. Countries after the 1444 Divergence (page_id=1100, revision_id=32841) lists Khatalashya only under “Aspiring Polities” and cannot substantiate its history or formation rules. Two player posts are also retained.

For full source paths and recorded conflicts, see the evidence page.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Karassk (L68) — Karassk Ideas

Set ID: L68_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = L68 #Karassk
    }

Karassk Traditions

  • Aggressive expansion impact: -10% (ae_impact; raw value -0.1).

  • Light ship cost: -10% (light_ship_cost; raw value -0.1).

1. The Emerald Of The Seas

The first of the Godseeker line came to power in Karassk as the clock ran out in the final hours of the 332nd empire. Jessk Godseeker came unto the city with a great emerald whose beauty she said would light the way for the empire to come.

Placed atop a great lighthouse, its refractions made Karassk a beacon for trade in the literal sense of guiding ships to safety, but it also made sure Karassk formed the core of new trade links that formed the basis for the Karassian Empire.

Karassk became the Emerald of the Seas because it shone brightly and placed itself as the antithesis of its rising rival in Zerat. Karassk would flex the sinews of trade while Zerat clung to waging war for the sinew as a mere end.

  • Trade range: +25% (trade_range_modifier; raw value 0.25).

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

2. Claim Of The Sea Kings

At the height of the Karassian Polity, when it was wondered if they would be the ones to take the mantle of the 333rd and Final Empire and cast down Zerat, in the great harbour of Karassk city a great work was commissioned that would display for all to see the majesty of the empire this city built.

Upon the seafloor was laid a mosaic of coloured pieces, so that when the weather was good and the sea calm, sailors leaning over the sides of their ships would see a map of all the distant ports to which they travelled under the banner of Karassk.

Today the old subjects deny their place; the Vyzemby, the isles of South Sarhal and Far Kedwal all forget to send the tribute they still owe. They might have forgotten now, but the hope persists within Karassk that the fleets will sail once more and remind them of their place in the coming empire.

  • global_autonomy: -0.05% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.05).

3. Ashakada

The ancient Ashakada system was a levy under which coastal settlements would provide a share of those who had drawn blood each year to the Karassk navy. The headsmen of every village would see the telltale signs of the Ashakada Sutna with the single red stripe on black sails.

The guilty would see that their time had come; if no true guilty existed or no duty was owed in a given year, then it was no great thing for a few guilty men to be found, or else created. Thus was earned the name of the Blood Duty, both for these unscrupulous recruitment practices and for the short lives that those claimed under the Ashakada would have.

If a conscript survived three engagements, he was dropped off in a distant port without any provided way home. Even those who managed to survive would often be forced to take the offer of a sailor’s wage to try and earn enough to make their own way. The Ashakada was a death sentence even when it technically ended, for once taken few ever saw their homes again.

  • Sailor Modifier: +20% (global_sailors_modifier; raw value 0.2).

4. The Searching Fleet

The Searching Fleet is the pride and main flotilla of the Karassk forces, its mission on paper to be the vanguard of the efforts to search for Katesh. The lost goddess of the sea may no longer be our primary focus for worship, but our legends still hold that her efforts gave us the coves and bays that make our land suited to shipbuilding.

It was she who granted us the gift to communicate with the creatures of the sea, that they might aid our construction and work in tandem with our sea-bonded captains in the midst of combat, or to carry our vessels when the wind forsakes our fleet. Her gifts remain even after her departure to the deepest depths of the ocean.

Our search now exists largely in name only, as the loss of our colonies and dominions make their restoration our priority above the fascinations of the past. Rumours still grip our imagination though; when the tales are told, every lizardfolk who sails the sea claims to have heard Katesh’s plea in the sounds of the waves or in the songs of the whales. To find her, someday soon.

  • Naval Force Limit Modifier: +20% (naval_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.2).

  • Naval Morale: +10% (naval_morale; raw value 0.1).

5. Azure Pyramid

The city of Karassk was built atop a base of imperial plunder. Human immigration as part of that success led to panic among the established orders, who were able to institute a ban on their presence within the core of the city. This ban was motivated primarily by fear of competition from emergent ‘Khair’ families that threatened the control of traditional lenders - a threat never truly posed by Vyzemby subjects.

This ban on the presence of humans didn’t stop them from using what already-accumulated wealth they had to buy up and renovate the most forgotten of the pyramid quarters of Karassk at the time, the Azure. Repression by lizardfolk elites forced them to find niches in less regulated areas of the economy. Smuggling and other illicit activity became a human domain and attempts by authorities to crack down found that all traces became aether. In such a way the Khair, the windborne, proved themselves well-named.

The Khair families and the Azure Pyramid became a new hub for commerce and the city government retained their old ordinances on humans in the city centre - even as they brought this illicit economic activity into the fold and benefited from new opportunities for mercantile wealth.

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

6. Sea Devils

The gift of Katesh, our communication with the aquatic creatures, affords us opportunities to make use of them in conjunction with our usual forces. The ability to act as trappers, scouts and to move about more quickly than those without access to such bonds gives our troops the ability to steal a march on the movements of our enemies, and to attack in ways that give us a distinct advantage.

Karassian forces are labelled as Sea Devils for these tactics - what seem like savage and underhanded techniques are simply good sense, adapted from our servants. These techniques go beyond simple cooperation, and have led to the creation of unique fighting styles. We see how our dragoons operate with the help of the shark, the eel or the dolphin and apply these principles on the tactical and strategic level.

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.1).

  • Marine force limit: +15% (allowed_marine_fraction; raw value 0.15).

7. Lashuan City

The Lashuan City is the name given to the strange floating city of stitched-together rafts and obsolete ships that bobs along the coast of our realm, under guard from our training fleets. It was started during the greatest height of the Karassian Empire under the tenth king of the Godseeker dynasty and has grown ever since, developing a slowly-growing permanent population of those addicted to the luxurious experience, who pay for lifetime berths on the Lashuan.

A collection of homes that serves as a mobile embassy for our vassals, allies and other visitors to our empire, its ability to move around the imperial core serves as both a way of showing the wealth of our people and as a diplomatic tool. A delegate understands viscerally their state of favour with the crown when Karassk is a stone’s throw away, yet for three full cycles now they have seen only the coast.

Even with all this growth, the Lashuan City has never been forced to evict a diplomatic resident for space, and the Godseeker lineage keeps it well funded to make sure this never comes.

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

Karassk Bonus

  • Ship trade power: +25% (global_ship_trade_power; raw value 0.25).

Khatalashya (S81) — Khatalashyan Ideas

Set ID: S81_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = S81 #Khatalashya
    }

Khatalashyan Traditions

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.10).

  • Province warscore cost: -15% (province_warscore_cost; raw value -0.15).

1. The Final Empire

Lizardfolk history is analogous to a river. It twists and bends as the water flows towards its mouth. Some sections are violent, the water thrashing against its banks as war engulfs the latest lizardfolk empire. Some are peaceful as the water flows calmly through eras without conflict. But even at the river's widest point, it cannot compare to the ocean at the end. Each empire before us is but a minor meander in the lizardfolk timeline. We are its destination. We are the final form. We are the ocean. We are the 333rd Empire!

  • Administrative efficiency: +5% (administrative_efficiency; raw value 0.05).

2. Craftsmen Dynasties

The jewels of lizardfolk culture are its great cities. Not necessarily for the wondrous architecture, but for the craftspeople who live within them. The walls of every blacksmith are caked with the history of a thousand blacksmiths before them. The same is true of every bakery, every jeweller, every tannery, every dockyard, and every other building where a skilled craftsperson plies their trade. Their knowledge is carefully compiled and recorded, then passed down to their children and apprentices to carry on their profession. While the cities themselves may have traded hands hundreds of times over the millennia, the knowledge within them is retained.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.10).

  • [Country.GetBurghersName] Loyalty Equilibrium: +5% (burghers_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.05).

3. The Naga

The divine power of the naga means they have historically played a significant part in lizardfolk society. From minor roaming tribes guided by a single naga, to the vast empires of old with hundreds of naga making decisions as a high council, they have often had important, senior positions amongst our people. This has been the cause of many conflicts, sometimes even tearing empires apart, as the interests of the naga clashed with that of the nobility. That changes with our empire. We will clarify exactly what the role of nagas are in our society. Never again shall this uncertainty tear us apart.

  • Missionaries: +1 (missionaries; raw value 1).

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

4. The Jungle Cities

What makes the 333rd Empire so powerful is that it draws from the 332 empires that came before. The great lizardfolk cities that stand today are testament to that. However, for the many great lizardfolk cities standing today, there are ten times as many hidden deep in the jungle’s undergrowth. We should uncover these cities and rebuild them back to their former glory.

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Centre of trade upgrade cost: -15% (center_of_trade_upgrade_cost; raw value -0.15).

5. Lessons of the Past

If you want to start an argument with a lizardfolk, point out the impossibility of counting 333 empires across history. They will assure you that generations of chroniclers have been documenting each empire’s rise and fall across time. That much is certainly true, but getting any of those chroniclers to agree with each other, or agreeing on an interpretation of what they wrote, is another question entirely.

For example, if you were to take all primary and secondary sources deemed "official" by the naga, there were five empires all active at the same time from the 214th to the 219th. Or there’s the part where the emperor Haksals was midway through the declaration of the 90th empire before a spear was hurled through his skull and the 91st empire was declared, meaning the 90th empire lasted a whole 12 seconds. One area where this careful recording has helped, however, is that one can learn a lot about what not to do when running an empire from reading about how 332 previous empires collapsed.

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +15% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.15).

6. Lizardfolk Mutations

Most lizardfolk mutations are considered to be blessings by the gods. The naga are the most famous, with their shape and powerful magical abilities being considered a blessing from the god Naga-Khatesh. But their armies too have been filled with mutated lizardfolk, such as the powerful crocfolk whose thick scales swords bounced off of. Bullets, however, do not bounce off scales.

Thus, the armies of the 333rd Empire adapted. The bow-legged speedy iguanafolk, who historically acted as messengers rather than soldiers due to their lack of claws or strength, became the premier flanking ranged troops, as their low-lying figures made them hard to aim hit with musket fire and their guns were very light. The crocfolk donned plated steel armour battle suits with mounted miniature cannons, turning them into furious one-lizard armies that could destroy a brigade of humans by themselves. All lizardfolk mutations can find their place in the armies of the 333rd Empire.

  • fire_damage_received: -15% (fire_damage_received; raw value -0.15).

7. Enemies Within

It has been said the third-greatest enemy of the lizardfolk are the armies of Kheterata, the second-greatest are the terrible dragons, and the greatest enemy is his neighbour. The 333rd Empire sought to change that dynamic, with every lizardfolk working together for the glory of the empire. To do that though, the lizardfolk needed a way to brand any internal opposition as enemies that needed to be crushed.

The Freishar Incident gave them their enemy: the hags. History is filled with tales of the hags corrupting an ambitious ruler with promises of great power, and the governor Freishar was just another in a long line of those who made a bargain with the hags to seize power. With his treachery revealed and rebellion crushed, it was announced that anyone opposing the empire’s rule was in league with the hags. Whether they were actually in league with the hags did not matter. Constant vigilance had to be maintained.

  • global_spy_defence: +20% (global_spy_defence; raw value 0.20).

  • Yearly corruption: -0.1 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.1).

Khatalashyan Ambitions

  • Missionary strength: +3% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.03).
